desc: The Sol Foundation is the institution that turned the technical layer into a policy actor. Co-founded by Stanford's Garry Nolan and anthropologist Peter Skafish - reported as 15 August 2023, though the foundation's own About page gives 2022 - it describes its work as 'science, policy, and public education for the post-UAP world' across scientific and philosophical research, government and social policy, and public education. Its programme list is concrete: a Distributed UAP Observation Project, a Distributed Passive Radar Project, a UAP Image Analysis Team, a Nonhuman Intelligence Project, and citizen science. Its leadership is Skafish as Executive Director, Nolan as Executive Director of the Board, Jennifer Preston as COO, Christian Peters as Associate Director of Research, and - the significant hire - Kirk McConnell, a 37-year Senate Armed Services and intelligence-committee staffer, as Senior Legislative Affairs Officer. It publishes a numbered white-paper and policy-briefing series that includes Tim Gallaudet on the maritime domain (March 2024), Helen McCaw on UK policy (May 2024), Skafish on executive-branch secrecy and harm to Congress (November 2024), Karl Nell's 'The UFO Enigma: A Call for US Government Disclosure' (May 2025), and in 2026 three numbered Science and Policy Briefings: Villarroel's pre-satellite-era plate evidence (No. 1, January 2026), McConnell on a UAP whistleblower restitution fund (No. 2, April 2026), and von Rennenkampff on the first peer-reviewed UAP materials analysis (No. 3, April 2026). In June 2026 its co-founders, its senior adviser Tim Gallaudet, its advisory board member Jacob Haqq-Misra and its production lead Ross Howard were named to the UAP Science Advisory Council; the foundation called this 'a fulfillment of its founding mission'. In under three years a private foundation went from formation to supplying a plurality of the US government's outside scientific advisers on the subject.

claims.text: The Sol Foundation publishes a numbered white-paper and policy-briefing series whose authors include Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet (US Navy, ret.), Colonel Karl E. Nell (ret.), Peter Skafish, Kirk McConnell, Helen McCaw, Rizwan Virk, Paul Thigpen and Marik von Rennenkampff.

Sol's Vol. 1 No. 6 paper of November 2024, by co-founder and executive director Peter Skafish, is titled 'The Prospect of Executive Branch Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Secrecy: The Harm to Congress and Potential Remedies' and argues that long-standing executive-branch secrecy may have concealed decades of UAP knowledge, research programmes and potentially retrieved technologies from Congress.

Sol published Colonel Karl E. Nell (retired), 'The UFO Enigma: A Call for US Government Disclosure,' in May 2025, framed around the effort to revive the UAP Disclosure Act in 2025 and establish an independent review body.

Sol Science and Policy Briefing No. 2, April 2026, is 'UAP Whistleblower Restitution Fund Would Incentivize Disclosures to Congress' by Kirk McConnell, and states that individuals considering disclosing information about classified executive-branch UAP programmes to Congress face significant retaliation including immediate loss of livelihood.

Sol Science and Policy Briefing No. 3, April 2026, describes the first peer-reviewed analysis of physical materials associated with a multi-witness UAP event, conducted by Stanford immunologist Garry P. Nolan and colleagues using atomic and isotopic analysis techniques.

Sol Science and Policy Briefing No. 1, January 2026, covers Beatriz Villarroel's finding that night-sky survey photographs taken between 1949 and 1957, before the satellite era, contain large numbers of temporary star-like points of light.

The Sol Foundation states that the UAP Science Advisory Council was announced by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence 'with the support of the FBI' and is led by Avi Loeb, a member of Sol's own advisory board.

Sol states that among the fourteen people named to the council were its co-founders Garry Nolan and Peter Skafish, its senior adviser Tim Gallaudet, and its advisory board member Jacob Haqq-Misra, and that Ross Howard, who leads production for the foundation, would lead communications for the council.

Sol states that the council 'reports to a higher-level UAP Governance Board, an interagency body coordinating across military, law enforcement, and intelligence community agencies' and that 'All data shared with the council will be unclassified.'

Sol characterises the appointments as 'a fulfillment of its founding mission,' adding that 'Sol can now share its insight to the highest levels of government deliberation about disclosure, amplifying our impact.'

The Skeptics Society's independent announcement of the council's formation names Garry Nolan and Peter Skafish as Sol Foundation co-founders and Tim Gallaudet as an appointee, corroborating Sol's own account of the membership.

Sol's June 2026 announcement states that the foundation 'was established in 2023 by Dr. Nolan and Dr. Skafish,' which conflicts with founding-year information the organisation has published elsewhere.
The Sol Foundation solicits membership and donations on its own site but names no donors, foundations or corporate supporters anywhere in its published material.

dossier.narrative:
The Sol Foundation is the closest thing the modern disclosure effort has to a think tank, and the useful way to read it is by its bibliography rather than its press. Its publication series is numbered, dated and authored, and the sequence tells you what the organisation actually decided to work on.

The first tranche in 2024 was scoping work. Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, US Navy retired, published 'Beneath the Surface: We May Learn More about UAP by Looking in the Ocean' in March 2024, arguing that transmedium UAP and unidentified submersible objects are the overlooked domain. The foundation itself published 'UAP in Crowded Skies' in the same month and 'Anomalous Health Threats: Health Security Considerations for UAP' in July. Helen McCaw wrote on UK policy implications in May 2024. Paul Thigpen wrote on the Catholic Church's likely response in July.

Then in November 2024 Peter Skafish, the foundation's executive director and co-founder, published 'The Prospect of Executive Branch Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Secrecy: The Harm to Congress and Potential Remedies.' That is the pivot. The subject is no longer whether UAP are anomalous; it is whether an executive-branch secrecy regime has concealed decades of knowledge, research programmes and potentially retrieved technologies from Congress itself, and what remedies exist. In May 2025 the series published Colonel Karl E. Nell, retired, on 'The UFO Enigma: A Call for US Government Disclosure,' framed around the effort to revive the UAP Disclosure Act.

By 2026 the series had become numbered Science and Policy Briefings and had acquired an author who is the point of the whole exercise. Briefing No. 2, April 2026, is 'UAP Whistleblower Restitution Fund Would Incentivize Disclosures to Congress,' by Kirk McConnell. McConnell is Sol's senior legislative affairs officer and spent thirty-seven years on the staff of the Senate Armed Services Committee. The paper's premise is stated at the top: individuals considering disclosing information about classified executive-branch UAP programmes to Congress face significant retaliation, including immediate loss of livelihood, and several senators have said so. That is a former SASC staffer, writing under a foundation's imprint, designing a financial instrument to overcome the deterrent that the special-access architecture places on contractor and government employees who might talk to his old committee. Briefings No. 1 and No. 3, both by Marik von Rennenkampff, cover Beatriz Villarroel's pre-satellite-era night-sky plate work and what the foundation describes as the first peer-reviewed scientific analysis of possible UAP materials, involving Garry Nolan.

That combination - a Stanford immunologist doing materials and biological analysis, a career Senate Armed Services staffer doing legislative design, an anthropologist doing the theory of secrecy - is why Sol belongs on this map. It is not a UFO group. It is a small institution that identified the mechanism, staffed against it, and published a remedy.

The consequence arrived in June 2026. Following what the foundation calls 'historic releases of government records about UAP encounters,' the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, with the support of the FBI, announced a UAP Science Advisory Council led by Avi Loeb, who sits on Sol's own advisory board. The foundation's announcement states that among the fourteen scientists and experts named were Sol co-founders Garry Nolan and Peter Skafish; Sol senior adviser Tim Gallaudet; and Sol advisory board member Jacob Haqq-Misra. Ross Howard, who leads production for the foundation, would lead communications for the council. The council reports to a higher-level UAP Governance Board, 'an interagency body coordinating across military, law enforcement, and intelligence community agencies,' and 'All data shared with the council will be unclassified.' The foundation's own framing is unambiguous about what it thinks happened: 'The appointment of Sol's co-founders, Admiral (ret.) Gallaudet and Dr. Jacob Haqq-Misra to the government's scientific advisory body is a fulfillment of its founding mission. Sol can now share its insight to the highest levels of government deliberation about disclosure, amplifying our impact.'

Two things about that are worth holding separately. The first is a genuine institutional achievement: a private foundation went from formation to supplying a plurality of the government's outside scientific advisers on this subject in under three years. The second is a caution the board should apply without softening it: the council those people joined is, on the government's own description, unclassified-only. A body with no access to classified material cannot examine recovered material, cannot audit a carve-out special access programme, and cannot compel anything. Sol's own executive director wrote the paper explaining exactly why that matters. The organisation that best articulated the executive-branch secrecy problem has now placed its people inside a body that has been constituted on the far side of the secrecy line.

The last thing to say about Sol is the thing it does not say about itself. Its site solicits membership and donations. It names no donors, no foundations and no corporate supporters. For an entity on a board whose organising question is who pays, that is the largest single documentary gap in its record, and it is not resolved by anything published as of this writing. There is also a small unresolved inconsistency in its own account of its founding date - the June 2026 announcement says the foundation 'was established in 2023,' which does not match every version the organisation has published.
openQuestions: Who funds the Sol Foundation. No donor, foundation or corporate supporter is named in any published Sol material, and there is no public filing reviewed here that discloses its revenue sources.

The foundation's own founding date is inconsistent across its publications (2022 in some material, 'established in 2023' in the June 2026 council announcement); the incorporation record has not been checked.
Whether any Sol principal or adviser holds or has held a security clearance or special-access indoctrination that would constrain what they can say about the concealment thesis they publish on.
Whether the McConnell whistleblower restitution fund proposal has been introduced in any legislative vehicle, and by whom.

What relationship, if any, exists between Sol and the government bodies its people now advise beyond the individual appointments - whether any contract, agreement, data-sharing arrangement or funding flows between the foundation and ODNI, AARO or the FBI.
dossier.whatItIs: The Sol Foundation is a private non-profit co-founded by Stanford pathology professor Garry Nolan and anthropologist Peter Skafish that describes its work as science, policy and public education for what it calls the post-UAP world. It runs observational and analytical research projects, publishes a numbered white-paper and policy-briefing series, and holds an annual conference. In June 2026 five people connected to it - both co-founders, a senior adviser, an advisory board member and its production lead - were named to the US government's UAP Science Advisory Council.
dossier.whyImplicated: Sol is the institution that converted the private technical layer into a policy actor with standing inside government. Its published output is not popular advocacy; it is a policy programme aimed squarely at the concealment mechanism, including a November 2024 paper by its own executive director on executive-branch UAP secrecy and the harm to Congress, a May 2025 paper by retired Colonel Karl Nell calling for US government disclosure, and an April 2026 briefing by its senior legislative affairs officer - a 37-year Senate Armed Services Committee staffer - proposing a whistleblower restitution fund to incentivise disclosures to Congress. Within under three years of formation, that programme placed a plurality of the members of the first standing outside scientific advisory body the US government has convened on this subject. The single largest gap in the Sol record is that it names no donors, and the board treats an unfunded map of a funding question as an open problem rather than a settled one.
